**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-171319, Reactome:R-HSA-6790901)

**Proposed mechanism:** DKC1 (HGNC:2878) —DISRUPTS→ telomerase complex assembly and function (REACT:R-HSA-69903); NOP10 (HGNC:8045) —DISRUPTS→ telomerase complex assembly and function (REACT:R-HSA-69903); telomerase complex assembly and function (REACT:R-HSA-69903) —LEADS_TO→ dyskeratosis congenita (HP:0001037); telomerase complex assembly and function (REACT:R-HSA-69903) —LEADS_TO→ hematologic abnormalities (HP:0011364); telomerase complex assembly and function (REACT:R-HSA-69903) —LEADS_TO→ oral leukoplakia (HP:0000208); telomerase complex assembly and function (REACT:R-HSA-69903) —LEADS_TO→ nail dystrophy (HP:0000955). Mutations in DKC1 (X-linked) and NOP10 (autosomal recessive) both impair the assembly and function of the telomerase complex, a critical pathway for telomere maintenance. This disruption leads to the characteristic features of dyskeratosis congenita, including hematologic abnormalities, oral leukoplakia, and nail dystrophy.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in DKC1 or NOP10 in individuals presenting with phenotypes distinct from the core dyskeratosis congenita spectrum, or the absence of telomere length abnormalities in patients with confirmed pathogenic variants in these genes. _(variant: The presence of common, benign variants in DKC1 or NOP10 in the gnomAD database that do not segregate with the disease in affected families.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of telomere maintenance defects in both forms of dyskeratosis congenita provides a unified therapeutic target. Strategies aimed at enhancing telomerase activity or compensating for its loss could potentially benefit patients with either genetic etiology.
